title: Dresser Formation stromatolites, Pilbara
summary: Rocks of the Dresser Formation at the North Pole Dome in the Pilbara of Western Australia, about 3.48 billion years old, contain stromatolites: layered structures interpreted as built by microbial communities, including in hot-spring settings. They are among the oldest widely cited traces of life, though ancient biogenic signals are inherently hard to prove.

uncertainty.note: Sources give the age as ca. 3.48 Ga without an error range in the passages read; zeros here mean not stated, not exact.

where.modern_name: Dresser Formation, North Pole Dome, Pilbara Craton, Western Australia
where.historical_name: No polity; Paleoarchean volcanic-sedimentary terrane of the Pilbara Craton

paleo.not_applicable: Age of 3.48 Ga is beyond the 1000 Ma limit of the GPlates plate models.

importance.justification: Among the oldest proposed evidence of microbial life on Earth, and a reference site for judging how early life is recognised in rock.
